The 2-CPU cap alone, which leaves four workers competing for two cores, pulls xs's time to within 5% of rsync's or behind it, unlike the plain link where xs led by 1.39x.
Under lab2's latency and a 2-CPU sender, xs -a -j4's lead over rsync on a fresh real-congress copy shrinks from the plain link's 1.39x (J1d) to a loss of at least 5%.

Copying psample locally from NVMe to the T5 with cold caches, xs -aH is faster than rsync -aH and cp -a, and near a single tar stream.

trees.question: Does keeping more parent directories open make xs's receives faster than its parent, and than rsync, on the Mac and on Linux?

neo-ssd is idle with the full 6 h. Its link is local, so it cannot add latency, but it can hold neo to 2 CPUs. That tests, with no network involved, whether the CPU cap alone erodes xs's lead on the two home corpora behind lab2's gaps. The plain-link baselines are J2 for real-congress (rsync 1.84x slower) and LC1/LC12 for real-psample (xs about 10% behind, cold). The plan uses about 130 min and does not touch the waiting T16 nodes.
Can xs beat rsync -aH at copying psample from the Pi's NVMe to the T5?

earlier_plans: The mac runner is unreachable, so all new work goes to the idle neo-ssd runner, which has the full 6 hours. The plan tests whether xs beats rsync on the local psample backup when both use eager writeback, and confirms xs if it wins. It also covers the 1% re-sync cell that LC4 never reported, and checks whether eager writeback combines with --no-atomic. Together these use about 352 of the 360 available minutes, counting the possible confirmation.

Both lab2 gaps, congress-sample fresh and real-projects fresh (rsync ahead and neither proven), are taken to step 1: reproduction at home. neo races xs e51c1df1329a with lab2's flags (-a -j4) against rsync -a over the neo-mars link with 11 ms added and neo held to 2 CPUs. It splits the congress cell into a CPU-only arm and adds a plain-link psample baseline, and an 8-block confirmation of rsync's lead is attached wherever rsync screens at least 5% ahead, so a loss can be shown to repeat. neo-ssd checks whether the 2-CPU cap alone, with no network, erodes xs's lead locally on the same two home corpora; no development case is opened until a gap reproduces.
